# Modern Next.js Architecture and Recommended Development Approach

## Summary
For a new production app in 2026, use the **App Router** on current Next.js (16.x) with **React Server Components by default**, small `"use client"` boundaries, **Server Actions** for in-app mutations, **Route Handlers** for external HTTP APIs, explicit opt-in caching (`fetch` cache options or `use cache` + `cacheLife`/`cacheTag` with Cache Components), and the `create-next-app` defaults (TypeScript, Tailwind, ESLint, Turbopack). The **Pages Router remains supported but is not where new features land**; keep it only for stable maintenance apps or incremental migration.

## 1. App Router vs Pages Router: status and when each is valid

**App Router (`app/`) is the official default and recommended router for new projects.** `create-next-app` enables App Router by default and asks “Would you like to use App Router? (recommended)” ([Installation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/installation)).

**Pages Router (`pages/`) still ships, is not deprecated, and has no announced removal date.** Verified against Next.js 16 docs, guidance is: greenfield → App Router; maintenance-mode or tightly-deadlined active apps may stay on Pages Router without immediate technical risk ([2026 migration guide](https://arc.dev/employer-blog/nextjs-app-router-vs-pages-router/)).

Coexistence and upgrade are incremental by design: `app/` co-exists with `pages/` for page-by-page migration, and upgrading Next.js does not require adopting App Router ([App Router migration](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/migrating/app-router-migration)).

Practical rule:
- **New app:** App Router — no migration cost, where new features ship first.
- **Stay on Pages temporarily if:** app is in maintenance mode, deadline leaves no learning-curve budget, app is mostly interactive (`"use client"` everywhere anyway), or core dependencies have no Server Component story.
- **Migrate for:** nested-layout duplication, client fetch waterfalls, oversized client bundles, or need for streaming/metadata improvements ([2026 migration guide](https://arc.dev/employer-blog/nextjs-app-router-vs-pages-router/)).

## 2. Server Components, Client Components, and Server Actions

### Server-first component model
By default layouts and pages are Server Components. Use Client Components when you need state/event handlers (`onClick`/`onChange`), lifecycle (`useEffect`), browser-only APIs (`localStorage`, `window`), or custom hooks ([Server and Client Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components)).

Use Server Components when you need to fetch near the data source, keep secrets off the client, reduce shipped JavaScript, or improve FCP with progressive streaming. On the server Next.js renders Server Components to the RSC Payload and prerenders HTML; on first load HTML shows fast preview, RSC Payload reconciles trees, and JavaScript hydrates Client Components ([Server and Client Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components)).

Composition rules to enforce:
- Keep `"use client"` low and small — marking a large parent pulls its imports into the client bundle.
- Props from Server to Client must be serializable.
- To wrap server UI in client interactivity (providers, modals, expand/collapse), pass Server Components as `children`/props from a parent Server Component rather than importing them inside the Client file. Context providers themselves must be Client Components ([Server and Client Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components)).

### Server Actions for mutations
A Server Action is a React Server Function (`'use server'`) invoked via `<form action>`, `<button formAction>`, or client `startTransition`. It runs as a POST against the invoking page and, when it triggers immediate revalidation, returns both the action value and a re-rendered RSC Payload in one roundtrip. Treat every action as an untrusted entry point: authenticate/authorize and validate inputs inside the action ([Server Actions](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/server-actions)).

Use Server Actions for mutations triggered inside the app (forms, buttons that change state, `useActionState`/`useFormStatus` pending UI, `revalidatePath`/`revalidateTag`/`updateTag` + `redirect` as needed). Use Route Handlers when you need an HTTP endpoint for external callers (webhooks, mobile, public API) or GET caching. Forms with Server Actions support progressive enhancement ([Server Actions guide 2026](https://makerkit.dev/blog/tutorials/nextjs-server-actions)).

Security/deployment notes: CSRF origin check, 1MB default body limit, encrypted action IDs/closure variables, stable `NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` across instances, and rolling deploys to avoid “Failed to find Server Action” on stale clients ([Server Actions](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/server-actions)).

## 3. Current data-fetching, caching, and rendering model

### Uncached-by-default since v15
Without Cache Components, `fetch` requests are not cached by default; opt in with `cache: 'force-cache'` ([Previous caching model](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components)). The extended `fetch` modes are `auto no cache` (default: build-time fetch if prerenderable, otherwise per-request), `no-store` (always per-request), and `force-cache` (server-cache lookup), plus `next.revalidate`/`next.tags` lifetimes ([fetch API](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch)). This flipped from the aggressive cache-by-default of 13/14 because of stale-data confusion; Next.js 16 keeps fetch uncached by default ([Next.js 16 caching explained](https://lamebrown.dev/blog/nextjs-16-caching-explained)).

### Cache Components (Next.js 16) + PPR + ISR
With `cacheComponents: true`, data fetching is dynamic by default and you choose what to cache with the `use cache` directive on functions/components, paired with `cacheLife`/`cacheTag`. Uncached or runtime data (`cookies()`, `headers()`, `searchParams`) must sit inside `<Suspense>` and streams at request time. This Suspense-shell + streaming-dynamic model is Partial Prerendering (PPR) as the default ([Caching with Cache Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/caching)).

For ISR, `generateStaticParams` prerenders listed URLs; other URLs serve the instant App Shell then upgrade in the background and cache for next visitors — the equivalent of Pages `fallback: true`. `getStaticProps + revalidate` maps to `use cache + cacheLife`; `getStaticPaths` maps to `generateStaticParams` ([ISR with Cache Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components)).

Implication: do not rely on implicit caching. Decide per fetch/function: cache single API reads with `next.revalidate`/`tags` or `use cache` + profiles, invalidate with `revalidateTag`/`updateTag`/`revalidatePath`, and design dynamic holes with `Suspense`/`loading.tsx`.

## 4. Legacy vs current and new-production recommendation

### Legacy → current map
- `getServerSideProps` / `getStaticProps` / `getInitialProps` → `async` Server Components with `fetch` (plus cache choice); `getStaticPaths` → `generateStaticParams` ([App Router migration](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/migrating/app-router-migration)).
- `pages/_app.js` + `pages/_document.js` → single `app/layout.js` root layout; `pages/_error.js` → granular `error.js`; `pages/404.js` → `not-found.js`; `pages/api/*` → `route.js` Route Handlers on Web Request/Response ([App Router migration](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/migrating/app-router-migration)).
- `pages/about.tsx` → `app/about/page.tsx`; API routes → `app/api/.../route.ts`; `next/head` → `metadata`/`generateMetadata` ([Pages to App Router map](https://versions.dev/modernize/nextjs/pages-router-to-app-router)).
- `next/router` (`useRouter`, `pathname`, `query`, `router.events`) → `next/navigation` (`useRouter`, `usePathname`, `useSearchParams`) in Client Components.
- Next.js 16: `middleware.ts` deprecated → `proxy.ts` on Node.js runtime (keep `middleware.ts` only for Edge-runtime need); Turbopack is default for `dev`/`build` (`--webpack` to opt out); `next/legacy/image`, `images.domains`, and single-arg `revalidateTag(tag)` deprecated ([Next.js 16](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16)).

### Recommended new production setup
Start from `create-next-app@latest --yes`: App Router, TypeScript-first, Tailwind, ESLint (or Biome), Turbopack, `@/*` alias, `AGENTS.md`; requires Node.js 20.9+ ([Installation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/installation)). Then:

1. **Structure:** `app/` with nested `layout.tsx`/`page.tsx`/`loading.tsx`/`error.tsx`/`not-found.tsx`, route groups `(marketing)`/`(dashboard)` for different shells, `generateStaticParams` + `generateMetadata` for dynamic/SEO routes.
2. **Rendering:** Server Components default; push `"use client"` to leaf interactive components; providers as small client wrappers around `children`.
3. **Data:** fetch directly in Server Components; set caching explicitly per route (`force-cache`/`revalidate`/`tags` or `use cache` + `cacheLife`/`cacheTag`); wrap per-request parts in `Suspense`; use `connection()` + boundary for per-request values when on Cache Components.
4. **Mutations/APIs:** Server Actions + `useActionState` + Zod validation + `revalidatePath`/`updateTag` for in-app writes; Route Handlers (`route.ts` with `GET`/`POST`/etc.) for webhooks/external APIs; `proxy.ts` for network-boundary redirects/rewrites/auth gating, business authz in handlers/actions.
5. **Hygiene:** `await` all `cookies()`/`headers()`/`params`/`searchParams` (sync access removed in 16), use `images.remotePatterns`, `next/image`, two-arg `revalidateTag(tag, profile)` or `updateTag` in actions, and run `upgrade` codemods when bumping majors ([Next.js 16](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16)).

**Bottom line:** build new production apps on App Router server-first as above; do not start new work on Pages Router unless protecting a frozen legacy codebase, and then isolate new work in `app/` for incremental migration.

# OpenCut macOS Desktop App: Official vs Source vs Third-Party vs Community Claims

**Verdict: No — OpenCut currently has no usable official macOS desktop application.** Official distribution is a web app. Native desktop code exists but is an early, featureless shell. The only macOS DMG claim found is an unofficial fork that is currently unverifiable.

## 1. Official releases: web-only, no macOS installer

OpenCut's official site presents it as a browser-based editor — “Works on any platform” with “Try early beta” leading to web projects, offering no macOS DMG, installer, or Mac App Store download ([OpenCut.app](https://opencut.app/)).

The official repo describes OpenCut as “a free and open source video editor for web, desktop, and mobile,” but immediately qualifies this as a rewrite in progress: `opencut.app` still runs the classic web version, the rewrite lives separately until ready, and desktop/mobile from a shared Rust core is listed as “What's coming,” not a current release ([OpenCut-app/OpenCut](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)).

The latest official release notes confirm this. v0.3.0 lists only web-editor features — masks, keyframe graph editor, volume/speed, preview zoom, stickers — while explicitly stating: `apps/desktop/` “is a new GPUI + Rust app. It is early: there is a `main.rs` and a working build setup, but no features yet” ([v0.3.0 release](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/releases/tag/v0.3.0)).

No official DMG, Homebrew cask, or Mac App Store entry was found.

## 2. Source-buildable code: empty window on macOS, usable editor is web-only

Official structure is `apps/web/` Next.js web app plus `apps/desktop/` native GPUI app marked “in progress,” with desktop explicitly “opt-in” — “If you're only working on the web app, skip this entirely” ([opencut-classic archive README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic)).

The official desktop README states:

> Built with GPUI. Very early. Right now this is just a window that opens. ([desktop README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/apps/desktop/README.md))

Build commands are only `cargo run / check / build --release` via `moon run desktop:*`. Platform requirement is listed as “macOS: Xcode command line tools (Metal renderer)” ([desktop README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/apps/desktop/README.md)).

In practice, macOS contributors report Command Line Tools alone fail because GPUI compiles `shaders.metal` with `xcrun metal`, which needs full Xcode, and on Xcode 16.3+ also needs a ~688 MB `MetalToolchain` download — after which “the window opens,” still with no editor ([Issue #839](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/839)).

The usable editor is web code: `bun install` + `bun dev:web` serving localhost:3000, or `docker compose up` serving a production build at localhost:3100 ([opencut-classic archive README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic)). That is self-hosting a website, not a macOS app bundle.

## 3. Third-party packaging/forks: unofficial DMG claim, currently unverifiable

The only packaged-macOS claim found is `opencut-desktop-app/opencut`, which advertises:

> Mac → `OpenCut.dmg`, drag to Applications. Notarized, universal (Apple Silicon + Intel) ([opencut-desktop-app/opencut](https://github.com/opencut-desktop-app/opencut)).

The same project declares itself “a packaged build and AI-extended fork of OpenCut (`OpenCut-app/OpenCut`)” and “Independent project — not affiliated with the OpenCut core team” ([opencut-desktop-app/opencut](https://github.com/opencut-desktop-app/opencut)). It is therefore third-party by its own definition, not official, even if its marketing says “real OpenCut plus our AI layer.”

Crucially, direct fetches of that repo and its README returned 404 at research time ([opencut-desktop-app/opencut](https://github.com/opencut-desktop-app/opencut)). Treat any cached DMG claim as **unverified and potentially unsafe** — availability, signing/notarization, and contents could not be confirmed from the live repo. Do not install based on6134 badges or mirrors alone.

A WebCatalog “OpenCut - Desktop App for Mac & Windows” hit is namesake confusion: it points to opencut.ai (AI image generation), not the opencut.app video editor, with an explicit non-affiliation disclaimer ([WebCatalog listing](https://webcatalog.io/en/apps/opencut)).

## 4. Community claims vs maintainer position

Community treats usable desktop as a request, not reality:

- Feature request for a standalone executable/CapCut-equivalent desktop app suggests Electron packaging; maintainer reply says desktop “is already being worked on internally - not Electron, we’re going with a native approach” ([Issue #713](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/713)).
- An open pivot proposal argues web-first cannot serve pro workflows — 500GB media, NAS/shared storage, ProRes/DNxHR, camera RAW SDKs, hardware acceleration — and urges focusing on “Rust Core + Rust Desktop application” as the future ([Issue #881](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/881)).

In short: users asking “where is the Mac app?” are pointing to roadmap; maintainers agree native desktop is future work.

## Practical guidance for macOS users

- For usable OpenCut today, use the browser at the official site or self-host the web app ([OpenCut.app](https://opencut.app/), [self-host docs](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic)).
- Building `apps/desktop` on macOS today yields only a test window, not an editor ([desktop README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/apps/desktop/README.md), [Issue #839](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/839)).
- Do not confuse unofficial DMGs or opencut.ai listings with official releases ([opencut-desktop-app/opencut](https://github.com/opencut-desktop-app/opencut), [WebCatalog listing](https://webcatalog.io/en/apps/opencut)).

## Remaining uncertainties

- The unofficial fork’s DMG could reappear, move, or exist on mirrors; safety/signing could not be verified due to 404.
- Absence of Homebrew/Mac App Store entries is based on targeted searches, not an exhaustive store crawl.
- Timeline for a usable official native macOS app is undisclosed; “native in progress” is the only maintainer commitment.

# OpenCut as Foundation for Agent-Driven Video Editing in OpenCode — Viability Assessment

## Executive verdict: No — not currently

OpenCut (OpenCut-app/OpenCut) is MIT-licensed and highly visible (~89.4k stars, ~8.8k forks), but its main branch is in a full ground-up rewrite. The stable classic editor is frozen in an archived repo while all agent-relevant capabilities are unchecked roadmap items — not shipped foundations ([OpenCut repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)).

Building an agent-driven workflow inside OpenCode on OpenCut today would mean forking frozen browser code plus maintaining a fragile Playwright sidecar, against a moving rewrite that explicitly is not accepting outside contributions. The pragmatic agent path in OpenCode today is deterministic CLI/code-driven rendering (FFmpeg, Remotion/video-as-code, or FFmpeg+MCP designs), with OpenCut revisited only after its Rust-core headless + versioned MCP/plugin API lands.

## 1. Project status, maturity, licensing

OpenCut is described as a free open-source editor for web, desktop and mobile under MIT ([OpenCut repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)).

Critical changed assumption vs. “mature CapCut alternative” narrative:

- **Rewrite in progress:** “OpenCut is being rewritten from the ground up … previous version at opencut-app/opencut-classic, which is the one to reach for today” ([OpenCut repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)).
- **Classic archived:** The original codebase is explicitly “archived and no longer maintained. The rewrite is happening at opencut-app/opencut” ([opencut-classic](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic)).
- **Contribution freeze:** “We’re not set up to take outside contributions yet while the architecture is being designed” ([OpenCut repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)).
- **Future promise vs. present:** Editor API, plugin-first architecture, single Rust core, MCP server for AI agents, headless mode and scripting tab are listed as “What’s coming” ([OpenCut repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)), and tracked as unchecked TODOs requiring engine/UI separation first ([rewrite tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)).

Implication: any “build on main today” assumption is wrong. Choice is (a) fork archived classic, or (b) bet on incomplete rewrite.

## 2. Production viability for real workloads

Classic can do short-form browser edits but is not production-robust:

- **Formats:** MP4 and WebM (VP9) with quality presets and project fps (24/30/60); docs warn speed depends on length/quality/CPU/complexity and “long projects, consider exporting overnight” ([export docs](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/features/export)).
- **Pipeline:** Exporter goes through mediabunny delegating to WebCodecs VideoEncoder/AudioEncoder; where those APIs are missing export fails without fallback. The fallback is MediaRecorder-based, real-time (60s timeline ≈ 60s) and WebM-only ([export fallback PR](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/pull/797)).
- **Browser architectural limits:** WASM fallback ~10x slower without hardware acceleration, 4GB WASM linear-memory cap, GC/compositor dropped frames, GPUDevice loss requiring pipeline rebuild, background-tab throttling stalling long exports, and no CUDA/OptiX/TensorRT or direct CoreML ([browser-limits discussion](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/881)).
- **Prototype status:** Guidance explicitly says avoid preview/export work because “current preview renders DOM elements (HTML), but we’re moving to binary rendering … current HTML-based preview is essentially a prototype” ([contributing notice](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/fbe3db74/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md)).

For OpenCode agents that expect headless, batch, repeatable renders, browser-tab fragility and real-time fallback are disqualifying for anything beyond demos.

## 3. Can agents programmatically drive OpenCut today?

No official surface exists:

- Official tracking lists Editor API, plugin system, MCP server, headless mode and scripting as unchecked, with “separating the engine from the UI” as prerequisite ([rewrite tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)).
- The only in-repo programmatic hook is in-page: `EditorCore.getInstance().renderer.exportProject({format, quality, includeAudio})` via RendererManager — a browser in-page API, not a headless/CLI service ([RendererManager docs](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/api/renderer-manager)).
- A headless Rendering SDK proposal (Next.js standalone + headless Chromium via Playwright, DraftTemplate JSON + `opencut-render` CLI, reusing `exportProject` byte-identical) remains a proposal; review notes Rust crates cover only ~30% of pipeline (frame descriptors, 9 node renderers, Canvas2D text, mediabunny muxing still in TS), so Chromium dependency remains and “not something that lands quickly” ([headless proposal](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/778)).

Community proves possibility but also fragility:

- `opencut-controller` exposes 161 MCP tools via Playwright injecting into the browser, but “requires the Legacy OpenCut (Next.js App Router) … Use the archived legacy repo” and “You must run the OpenCut editor locally. The production site doesn’t expose the internal hooks” ([opencut-controller](https://github.com/JXUE0/opencut-controller)).
- Minimal `opencut-mcp` targets a fork with patches exposing `window.__editor` (EditorCore) and MediaTime helpers, validated only at pinned commit `a7443ec8`, dev-mode only, commit-level compatibility ([opencut-mcp](https://github.com/kenimo49/opencut-mcp)).

In short: agent control today = patch + run browser locally + drive via `page.evaluate`. Workable for a demo, not a foundation.

## 4. Integration inside OpenCode and alternatives

OpenCode (Go CLI/TUI) supports MCP via stdio subprocess and SSE, with `mcpServers` config and permission model where MCP tools appear alongside built-ins ([OpenCode repo](https://github.com/opencode-ai/opencode)).

Technically you could register a community OpenCut MCP server as a stdio server in OpenCode. Practically it violates OpenCode expectations:

- Requires sidecar stack: local Next.js classic + Playwright Chromium + patched fork, because production exposes no hooks ([opencut-controller](https://github.com/JXUE0/opencut-controller)).
- Adds 200MB+ Chromium, 5s startup, focus/throttling risk, and maintenance on frozen code.

Architecturally closer alternatives for OpenCode agents:

- **Deterministic FFmpeg+MCP:** OmniCut composes real footage via FFmpeg with 29–31 MCP tools, shared project store between GUI and MCP server, rendering deterministic H.264/AAC via bundled ffmpeg-static ([OmniCut](https://github.com/WillBe89/omnicut)).
- **Video-as-code:** The unrelated `floomhq/opencut` model treats timeline as TypeScript, with CLI `opencut-render/validate/transcribe` and Remotion frame-accurate rendering — diffable, testable, CLI-driven, ideal for LLM structured output ([floomhq opencut](https://github.com/floomhq/opencut)).

Note on naming: `floomhq/opencut` is not OpenCut-app/OpenCut; it is included only as an architectural pattern reference.

If visual timeline UI is mandatory, keep OpenCut classic as a human preview UI fed by agent-generated JSON, but render canonically via FFmpeg/Remotion — do not make browser export the source of truth.

## 5. Real blockers: architectural vs. unfinished

**Mostly unfinished (would resolve with rewrite):**

- Missing Engine Core, stable Editor API, plugin API/host, headless mode, MCP server, scripting, public beta — all unchecked ([rewrite tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)).
- Contribution freeze and archived classic mean building now = forking dead code ([OpenCut repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut), [opencut-classic](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic)).

**Architectural (persists for classic path even with polish):**

- WASM without hardware accel, 4GB cap, GPUDevice loss, background throttling, no vendor ML extensions ([browser-limits discussion](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/881)).

This distinction matters: OpenCut is not a dead-end idea — Rust core + binary rendering + headless directly addresses the architectural side — but classic cannot be hardened into a server-grade agent renderer.

## 6. What evidence would change the recommendation

Flip from “no” to “pilot” or “yes” if observed in the canonical repo:

1. Shipped opt-in automation bridge (DraftTemplate/zod + CLI) with byte-identical headless export, without requiring 200MB Chromium/5s startup, and Rust pipeline covering well beyond current ~30% with text/layout/muxing parity ([headless proposal](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/778)).
2. Checked-off Engine Core + versioned Editor/MCP/plugin API + public beta in rewrite tracking ([rewrite tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)).
3. Removal of contribution freeze and un-archiving / stable maintenance of the line you would build on ([OpenCut repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)).
4. For limited scope only: if requirement is short browser demos and team accepts Playwright sidecar cost, community 161-tool coverage ([opencut-controller](https://github.com/JXUE0/opencut-controller)) could justify a throwaway prototype — not a foundation.

Watch `new.opencut.app` progress indirectly via main-repo checklist deltas, not star count.

## Recommendation

- **Do not adopt OpenCut-app/OpenCut as the foundation for an agent-driven workflow inside OpenCode today.**
- For production agents: use FFmpeg CLI scripts or Remotion-style video-as-code (or OmniCut-style FFmpeg+MCP pattern) where OpenCode’s stdio MCP and bash tools shine ([OpenCode repo](https://github.com/opencode-ai/opencode), [OmniCut](https://github.com/WillBe89/omnicut), [floomhq opencut](https://github.com/floomhq/opencut)).
- If investing in OpenCut: time-box to a disposable bridge experiment on a pinned classic fork, isolate rendering behind an interface so you can swap to the future Rust headless when it ships, and track the two flip signals above.
- Re-evaluate only on shipped headless + MCP, not on roadmap promises or stars.

# Best Practical OpenCode Video Stack for a Solo Developer — AI Video + Motion Graphics + Blender 3D + Edit + Audio + Captions + Render

## TL;DR — Simplest capable architecture today

**OpenCode orchestrates files, not live apps.** Keep every tool as a file-artifact exchange around two mature code-driven cores:

1. **HyperFrames for programmatic motion graphics / overlays / captions** — HTML composition + deterministic local render fits agents best: HyperFrames is an open-source Apache-2.0 framework that turns plain HTML/CSS/JS with data attributes into deterministic MP4 via headless Chrome + FFmpeg with no React/build step [(source)](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes).
2. **FFmpeg + thin Python for assembly and final render** — concat demuxer and single `filter_complex` invocation per render (trim/scale/overlay/xfade/drawtext/fps-normalize) without pulling frames into Python [(source)](https://github.com/tomastimelock/video-arrange), scriptable via Python bindings for complex graphs [(source)](https://github.com/kkroening/ffmpeg-python).

Treat everything else as vendors that drop files in:

* **AI video (Sora / Veo / Runway / Luma): async submit → poll → download MP4**, short clips only — Sora 4/8/12s, Veo 3.1 4/6/8s up to 4K with native audio, Runway 5/10s image-to-video [(source)](https://teachmeidea.com/sora-vs-veo-vs-runway/), e.g. Luma Ray 3.2 text/image-to-video with presigned MP4 expiring in 1 hour [(source)](https://docs.agents.lumalabs.ai/guides/videos/generation), Runway unified API/SDK + model router [(source)](https://dev.runwayml.com/).
* **Headless Blender for 3D artifacts only**: `blender --background` + `--python-expr` overrides without touching source `.blend` [(source)](https://harlepengren.com/blender-python-addon-scene-data-subprocess/), backed by mature `bpy` background/module automation [(source)](https://docs.blender.org/api/main/info_advanced_blender_as_bpy.html).
* **Audio/music/captions via API + human curation**: ElevenLabs TTS/STT/music/SFX with TS/Python SDKs [(source)](https://elevenlabs.io/api), music compose from prompt/plan e.g. `music_length_ms` [(source)](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/cookbooks/music.mdx), Whisper transcription with timestamps → TTS/mix pipeline [(source)](https://sync.so/docs/tutorials/video-translation-api-guide.mdx).
* **OpenCut only as human finishing NLE**: free MIT multi-track local-first editor [(source)](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/introduction) — do NOT couple OpenCode to its automation.

**Do not couple to immature interfaces:** OpenCut Editor API / headless / scripting / MCP are announced as coming in a ground-up rewrite, with classic as the usable version [(source)](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut); OpenCut today lacks a stable programmatic entry point [(source)](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/778). Blender Lab MCP is lightweight/experimental, manual 3-part setup, unguarded code exec [(source)](https://www.blender.org/lab/mcp-server/) with structural round-trip/timeout/node-brittleness limits [(source)](https://www.mixar.app/blender-agent/blender-mcp-guide).

## 1. Roles and maturity

### HyperFrames — agent-automate (core)
Mature for code-driven video. Skills teach the production loop (plan → HTML → seekable animation → lint/preview/render) for Claude Code/Cursor/Gemini/Codex-class agents [(source)](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes). Engine seeks each frame in headless Chrome (Puppeteer) and encodes with FFmpeg; adapters for GSAP/CSS/Lottie/Three.js/Anime.js/WAAPI plus catalog blocks, Studio preview, AWS Lambda/cloud rendering [(source)](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes).

Limit: short unnarrated design-led pieces under ~10s up to 30s (kinetic type, stat, chart, logo sting, lower-third, overlay); longer/narrated/multi-scene → general-video pattern, transparent WebM/MOV only for overlays [(source)](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/blob/68205dbb/docs/prompting/motion-graphics.mdx). Not a 3D renderer, footage generator, or full NLE.

### FFmpeg / code-driven processing — agent-automate (core)
Most mature layer. One declarative timeline → one `filter_complex` → one `ffmpeg` subprocess is reproducible and fast; log full argv per render [(source)](https://github.com/tomastimelock/video-arrange). `ffmpeg-python` handles arbitrarily large DAGs and verbatim custom filters [(source)](https://github.com/kkroening/ffmpeg-python). Use for concat, fps normalize, scale/pad, overlay/PiP, xfade, drawtext/captions burn-in, loudness, H.264/AAC delivery.

### Blender 3D — file-artifact exchange (selective automate)
Mature when scoped to: versioned `.blend` + versioned render script → `blender -b file.blend --python-expr ... -s/-e -a` → PNG sequence / MP4 / EXR artifact → FFmpeg/HyperFrames consume it [(source)](https://harlepengren.com/blender-python-addon-scene-data-subprocess/). `bpy` as module/background mode explicitly supports visualization, compositing, VSE, conversion, automation [(source)](https://docs.blender.org/api/main/info_advanced_blender_as_bpy.html).

Not coupled: live MCP driving. Official path needs Blender 5.1+, separate add-on + LLM client + MCP server and runs unguarded LLM code — VM only [(source)](https://www.blender.org/lab/mcp-server/). Bridges suffer: model sees only exposed tools, every op is a round-trip (slow/expensive long passes), heavy ops time out, Geometry/shader graphs brittle across versions, rigging out of reach [(source)](https://www.mixar.app/blender-agent/blender-mcp-guide).

Practical solo rule: agent writes small `bpy` scripts for primitives/materials/lighting/camera/turntable/product shots; human owns rigging, sculpt, complex nodes, look-dev, and final quality review.

### OpenCut — human-in-loop, not coupled
Role: cheap, private human timeline polish. Free MIT CapCut alternative, multi-track + real-time preview, videos stay on device [(source)](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/introduction).

Automation maturity: immature by design today. Rewrite promises Editor API, plugin-first Rust core, MCP, headless, scripting tab [(source)](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut), but programmatic SDK/headless proposals are still issues/RFCs requiring opt-in bridge + Playwright Chromium [(source)](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/778). Do not build OpenCode → OpenCut MCP/Playwright/`window.__editor` hacks into your critical path.

### AI video generation — file-vendor handoff (semi-automate)
All usable vendors share the same agent pattern: persist job/operation ID, poll/worker, download to own storage (presigned URLs expire; Google keeps ~2 days, Luma 1 hour), cap spend. Clip limits force stitching: Sora 4/8/12s, Veo 4/6/8s, Runway ~5/10s; Sora/Veo native audio, Runway Gen-4 silent [(source)](https://teachmeidea.com/sora-vs-veo-vs-runway/). Luma adds anchor/multi-keyframe image control [(source)](https://docs.agents.lumalabs.ai/guides/videos/generation). Runway image-to-video gives most deterministic brand/product control from a still first frame plus router/workflows/MCP [(source)](https://dev.runwayml.com/).

Cost discipline: ~$0.25–$3.50 per 5s across Lite/turbo drafts vs flagship Pro/4K [(source)](https://teachmeidea.com/sora-vs-veo-vs-runway/). Pattern: iterate Veo Lite / turbo / fast at 720p, re-render only approved hero at Pro/4K.

### Audio / music / captions / final render
Agent-scriptable, human-gated. ElevenLabs covers TTS, STT, music, SFX, dubbing, isolation via SDKs with per-char/per-min/per-generation billing [(source)](https://elevenlabs.io/api). Compose beds via prompt or composition plan [(source)](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/cookbooks/music.mdx). Captions: Whisper segments with timestamps → translate/correct → SRT/VTT → HyperFrames rail or FFmpeg burn-in; TTS cloning for localization [(source)](https://sync.so/docs/tutorials/video-translation-api-guide.mdx). Final: FFmpeg loudness (EBU R128), `-c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac`, 1080p masters + vertical crops; human watches once on phone + desktop before publish.

## 2. What to automate vs human vs file exchange vs not couple

**Agent-automated in OpenCode (deterministic, cheap to retry):**
* HyperFrames compositions: `init → lint → preview → render` from versioned `index.html` + `variables` templating.
* FFmpeg assembly: `timeline.toml/json → export_command() → ffmpeg → final.mp4` with logged argv + ffprobe checks.
* Vendor fetchers: `fetch_ai_clip.py`, `fetch_tts.py`, `fetch_music.py`, `transcribe.py` (Whisper) that write to `assets/` with manifests.
* Captions: `transcribe → correct → .srt → burn-in or HyperFrames rail`.
* QC scripts: duration/codec/resolution/loudness checks, thumbnail contact sheet.

**Human-in-loop (taste, legality, quality):**
* Prompt/casting approval for AI clips, voice/music selection, caption accuracy, brand/type review, Blender look-dev, final watch + loudness + export preset, thumbnail/title, publish.
* Keep one explicit gate: “preview first, or render?” then “draft or final?” before spending on Pro/4K or long renders.

**File-artifact exchange (contract between agent steps):**
* `brief.md` → `shots.json` (clip list with durations) → `assets/` (mp4/wav/srt/blend/html) → `timeline.toml` → `renders/` + `render.log` (full ffmpeg argv).
* Blender: `.blend` + `render_blender.py` → `blender_out/` (PNG seq + `clip.mp4`).
* AI video: `prompts/` + `jobs.json` (IDs) → `assets/ai/*.mp4` (local copy, never hotlink presigned URL).
* HyperFrames: `compositions/*/index.html` → `renders/overlay.mp4` or `transparent.webm` (overlay only).

**Not coupled (explicitly avoid today):**
* OpenCut Editor API / headless / MCP / scripting / Playwright `window.__editor` automation.
* Blender live MCP session as render backbone (OK for assisted inspection on a copy, not pipeline).
* Direct NLE project mutation from agent; instead export finished intermediates and finish by hand in OpenCut if needed.
* Cloud-render lock-in before local deterministic path works.

## 3. Minimal folder + commands (solo-dev starter)

```
video-project/
  brief.md
  shots.json
  prompts/
  assets/ai/  assets/audio/  assets/blender/  assets/captions/
  compositions/intro/  # hyperframes index.html
  blender/shots/       # .blend + render_blender.py
  scripts/assemble.py  # ffmpeg-python or declarative builder
  timeline.toml
  renders/
```

* `npx hyperframes init intro; npx hyperframes preview; npx hyperframes render . -q high -o renders/overlay.mp4`
* `blender -b blender/shots/hero.blend --python-expr "import bpy;..." -s 1 -e 120 -a`
* `python scripts/fetch_ai.py && python scripts/fetch_audio.py && python scripts/transcribe.py`
* `python scripts/assemble.py --manifest timeline.toml --dry-run; python scripts/assemble.py --manifest timeline.toml -o renders/final.mp4`
* Human: review `renders/final.mp4` in OpenCut if trim/polish needed; otherwise publish.

# Recommended Next.js Architecture for a New Production Application (September 2026)

## Executive summary
Start a new production app on **Next.js 16 LTS (App Router)** with TypeScript, Turbopack defaults, and `proxy.ts`. Keep `app/` routing-only, default to React Server Components, use explicit Cache Components (`use cache` + `cacheLife`/`cacheTag` + Suspense for Partial Prerendering), mutate via Server Actions with scoped revalidation, protect data via a Data Access Layer, and deploy via Vercel or hardened Node/Docker.

## 1. Baseline: version and router
Current stable is **Next.js 16 LTS (released Oct 2025; latest 16.3.5 as of 11 Sep 2026)**; 15.x is in maintenance until Oct 2026 ([endoflife](https://endoflife.date/nextjs)).

Use **App Router for all new projects**; `app` = App Router, `pages` = Pages Router legacy ([project structure](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure)).

Minimums for 16: Node.js 20.9+, TypeScript 5.1+, React 19.2; `next dev`/`next build` use Turbopack by default; React Compiler stable ([Next.js 16 announcement](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16)).

## 2. Project structure
Official conventions: required root `layout.tsx`, plus `page.tsx`, `loading.tsx`, `error.tsx`, `not-found.tsx`, `route.ts`; organize URLs without affecting paths via route groups `(marketing)`, `(shop)`, `(app)`; optional `src/` folder ([project structure](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure)).

Production pattern that works at scale:
- `app/` owns **routing and screen composition only**
- Shared/domain logic lives in `src/features/<domain>/` or `lib/<domain>/` (queries, mutations, schemas)
- Truly shared UI in `components/ui/`
- Colocate route-specific code with private folders `_components`, `_lib`
- Separate product areas with route groups `(marketing)` / `(app)` / `(admin)` for different layouts ([production App Router architecture](https://www.pean.dev/blog/nextjs-app-router-architecture-in-2026))

Do not add service/repository layers by default; add only to isolate real complexity or duplication.

## 3. Rendering, fetching, caching, mutations
### 3.1 Cache Components is the new default mental model
With `cacheComponents: true`, **nothing is cached by default**; all dynamic code runs at request time unless explicitly marked with `use cache` ([Next.js 16 announcement](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16)).

Apply `use cache` at data-level (fetch/compute functions) and UI-level (components/pages/layouts), always paired with `cacheLife`; cached output becomes part of the static shell / App Shell and prefetches ([caching guide](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/caching)).

Structure pages as: cached static shell + `<Suspense>` holes for dynamic/runtime parts = **Partial Prerendering (PPR)**, default with Cache Components.

Critical rule: **never read `cookies()`, `headers()`, `searchParams` inside a cached scope**; read outside and pass as arguments ([use cache reference](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)). Use `use cache: remote` for durable shared cache, `use cache: private` only for compliance/edge cases.

ISR with Cache Components: `generateStaticParams` prerenders known params; unknown URLs serve App Shell instantly then upgrade in background.

### 3.2 Components
Server Components by default for reads; `"use client"` only for interactive leaves. Enforce boundary with `server-only` imports + lint so DB code cannot leak to client.

### 3.3 Mutations
- **Server Actions (`'use server'`)** for UI-owned mutations: validate (Zod), authorize, write, then invalidate ([Server Actions guide](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/server-actions)):
  - `updateTag()` — immediate expiry, read-your-writes (Server Actions only)
  - `revalidateTag(tag, profile)` e.g. `'max'` — stale-while-revalidate
  - `revalidatePath()` — single path
  - `refresh()` — refresh uncached data only
- **Route Handlers (`route.ts`)** for real HTTP contracts: webhooks (Stripe), mobile/partner APIs, cron. Keep Stripe client reusable outside the route.

## 4. Application stack: styling, auth, data, forms
### Auth + authorization
Prefer an auth library; centralize checks in a **Data Access Layer** (`verifySession()` memoized with React `cache`), return DTOs, use Proxy only for optimistic redirects ([authentication guide](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/authentication)).

Choices in 2026 ([comparison](https://codecudos.com/blog/clerk-vs-authjs-vs-better-auth-nextjs-2026)):
- **Clerk** — fastest (afternoon), prebuilt UI, Organizations/RBAC, MFA/passkeys; pay per MAU, users on Clerk infra
- **Auth.js v5 (NextAuth)** — free self-hosted, battle-tested, own your data; build UI/orgs yourself
- **Better Auth** — self-hosted TS-first, orgs/2FA/passkeys/magic-links as plugins, Drizzle/Prisma adapters; best greenfield self-hosted default

Check auth per page/action/handler/DAL function — never Proxy/middleware alone; layouts don't re-render on navigation so page-level checks are required.

### Styling / data / forms
Standard production stack: **Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui (Radix), Drizzle (or Prisma) on Postgres (Neon/Supabase/Vercel Postgres), React Hook Form + Zod shared schema + type-safe Server Actions** (`next-safe-action` or `useActionState`) ([forms with Drizzle](https://makerkit.dev/docs/nextjs-drizzle/development-guide/working-with-forms)).

Single Drizzle client via `globalThis`, Zod-validated env (`@t3-oss/env-nextjs` or Zod `env.ts`), one barrel `index.ts` per feature.

## 5. Deployment and production hardening
- **Vercel**: zero-config, global ISR/CDN, Analytics + Speed Insights
- **Self-host** with `next start` Node/Docker behind reverse proxy (nginx) with streaming enabled (disable buffering), shared cache handler (Redis/S3) for multi-instance, same `NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` everywhere, `deploymentId` for version-skew protection ([self-hosting](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/self-hosting))
- Validate with `next build && next start`, test ISR hits/misses via `x-nextjs-cache`, monitor Core Web Vitals.

## 6. What to avoid in new apps (Next.js 16)
Rename `middleware.ts` → `proxy.ts` (function `proxy`, Node.js runtime only; keep `middleware` only if you need Edge) ([upgrade guide](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16)); `await` all `params`/`searchParams`/`cookies()`/`headers()`/`draftMode()`; pass `cacheLife` profile to `revalidateTag(tag, profile)`; replace `unstable_cache`/`fetch({next:{revalidate,tags}})`/`revalidate` segment config with `use cache` + `cacheLife`/`cacheTag`; use `images.remotePatterns` not `images.domains`; use `next/image` not `next/legacy/image`; remove `next lint`, AMP, `experimental.ppr`/`dynamicIO`; run `npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest` ([Next.js 16 announcement](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16)).

## Starter blueprint
```
my-app/
 app/
  (marketing)/ page.tsx about/page.tsx + layout.tsx
  (app)/ dashboard/page.tsx loading.tsx error.tsx [id]/page.tsx
  api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts
  layout.tsx global-error.tsx
 src/
  features/billing/{server,client,data,schema.ts,index.ts}
  features/auth/
  lib/{db.ts,env.ts,auth/dal.ts}
  components/ui/
 proxy.ts
 next.config.ts // { cacheComponents:true, turbopack:{...} }
```
Monorepo (Turborepo + pnpm) only when you have a second deployable; then `apps/*` + `packages/{ui,db,config}`.

## Remaining uncertainties
- `proxy.ts` Edge support roadmap is pending; Edge-dependent interception should stay on `middleware.ts` for now.
- Exact cache persistence costs (`use cache: remote`) are platform-specific.
- Auth pricing (Clerk MAU/MRU tiers) changes frequently — verify at build time.

# OpenCut Official Automation Interfaces — Current State

**Answer in brief:** OpenCut currently provides **no official public automation interfaces** — no public REST API, CLI, SDK, or webhooks. The official README lists Editor API, third-party plugins, MCP server, headless mode and scripting tab as “What’s coming” in a ground-up rewrite, with production still on the classic version ([OpenCut-app/OpenCut README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)).

## 1. What official automation interfaces exist today?

**None as public, stable automation products.**

- Official roadmap status: Editor API, plugin-first architecture, Rust core, MCP server for AI agents, headless mode for automation/batch rendering, and in-editor scripting tab are all listed as future work, not current offerings ([OpenCut-app/OpenCut README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)).
- Rewrite tracking confirms the same items — Editor API, Plugin API/design, Headless mode, MCP server, Scripting — as unchecked todos sharing a future Rust core engine ([Tracking: OpenCut rewrite #811](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)).
- A feature proposal explicitly states OpenCut “lacks a programmatic entry point” and proposes a new `render-sdk` library + CLI as not-yet-upstream, asking if direction is welcome upstream ([Headless Rendering SDK proposal #778](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/778)).
- Developer docs index contains only in-code editor APIs — EditorCore, managers, Actions, Commands, hooks — with no REST/CLI/SDK/webhooks section ([Mintlify docs index](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/llms.txt)).

> This means third-party MCP/controller projects and Python/CLI proposals found in search are unofficial and out of scope for “official” interfaces.

## 2. Capabilities, auth and limits

### Only automation-adjacent surface: internal contributor API

The only officially documented programmatic surface is the internal, in-process TypeScript editor framework:

- `EditorCore` central singleton coordinating managers for `playback, timeline, scenes, project, media, renderer, command, save, audio, selection`, accessed via `useEditor()` in React or `EditorCore.getInstance()` outside React ([EditorCore docs](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/api/editor-core)).
- `invokeAction()` unified trigger layer for user-initiated operations across playback, navigation, editing, selection, history and timeline — e.g. `toggle-play, split, delete-selected, undo/redo` — with `useActionHandler` bindings ([Actions docs](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/api/actions)).
- `TimelineManager` (`editor.timeline`) for add/remove tracks, insert/delete/duplicate/update/split/move/trim elements, clipboard paste, preview/commit/discard, duration queries; mutations auto-push to undo/redo unless `pushHistory: false` ([TimelineManager docs](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/api/timeline-manager)).

These are contributor extension points requiring a running editor codebase, not a stable external automation contract. Direct `editor.xxx()` calls are documented for internal use (commands/tests/multi-step ops), while `invokeAction()` is preferred for UX-integrated triggers.

### Auth / access / limits: not applicable

- No API keys, OAuth, base URLs, or rate limits are documented for automation because no public automation API exists.
- Documented secrets cover only self-hosted app operation: `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, DATABASE_URL, Redis, Freesound keys` for local dev ([Getting Started](https://opencut.dev/docs/getting-started/)).

## 3. Canonical documentation and currency

- Code + roadmap truth: [OpenCut-app/OpenCut README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut) — states rewrite in progress, classic in production, new preview site pending.
- Operator/dev setup: [OpenCut Documentation hub](https://opencut.dev/) and [Getting Started](https://opencut.dev/docs/getting-started/).
- In-code API reference: [Mintlify docs index](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/llms.txt), [EditorCore](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/api/editor-core), [Actions](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/api/actions), [TimelineManager](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/api/timeline-manager).
- Forward-looking design: [Tracking: OpenCut rewrite #811](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811) and [Headless Rendering SDK proposal #778](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/778).

All sources are consistent through the 2025–2026 rewrite period: automation is planned, not shipped. No material contradictions were found; experimental PRs and community MCP servers were excluded as unofficial.

**Practical implication:** If you need automation today, you must fork/patch the web app and drive internal `EditorCore`/`window.__opencut`-style hooks locally, or wait for the official Editor API / headless / MCP milestones. Do not expect official support, versioning, auth, or webhooks yet.

# Can you install a usable official OpenCut desktop app on macOS today? — No.

**Verdict:** There is no usable official OpenCut desktop application for macOS available for download today. The official desktop project is a very early developer-only shell with no editing features.

## 1. Does official OpenCut offer a macOS desktop build?

No downloadable end-user build is offered.

- The official project `OpenCut-app/OpenCut` describes itself as a free open-source editor for web, desktop and mobile, but states it is being rewritten from the ground up and that the previous/classic version at `opencut.app` is the one to reach for today ([official README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)).
- The latest official release notes for `v0.3.0` state: `apps/desktop/` is a new GPUI + Rust app that is early with only `main.rs` and a working build setup, but no features yet ([releases](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/releases), [v0.3.0](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/releases/tag/v0.3.0)).
- The official desktop README warns: Very early. Right now this is just a window that opens ([desktop README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/apps/desktop/README.md)).
- The official homepage offers no macOS `.dmg` download; it presents OpenCut as a web editor that works on any platform with Try early beta ([opencut.app](https://opencut.app/)).

Because there is no distributed installer, official supported macOS versions/architectures for end users are not published.

## 2. Can it be installed and used on macOS today?

Not as a usable editor. The only official macOS path is to compile the empty shell from source.

Installation method documented officially:

- Install pinned Rust via `proto use`, then `moon run desktop:dev` for `cargo run`, plus `desktop:check` and `desktop:build` for release builds ([desktop build instructions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/apps/desktop/README.md)).
- The first build compiles GPUI from source and takes a while, confirming there is no prebuilt installer ([desktop build instructions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/apps/desktop/README.md)).
- The classic-project variant describes the same opt-in developer flow: install Rust toolchain, run native-dependencies script, then `cargo run -p opencut-desktop` ([classic desktop README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic/blob/main/apps/desktop/README.md)).

macOS requirements for that shell:

- Xcode command line tools, for Metal renderer ([desktop README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/apps/desktop/README.md)).
- Classic setup notes the macOS script installs Xcode Command Line Tools if missing ([classic desktop README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic/blob/main/apps/desktop/README.md)).

Limitations:

- No features yet — only an empty window, so not usable for video editing.
- No official code-signing/notarization, versioned DMG, or system-version matrix is documented, because no end-user build is distributed.
- Latest context is `v0.3.0`, whose desktop part explicitly has no features ([v0.3.0](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/releases/tag/v0.3.0)).

What is usable officially instead is the web classic version at `opencut.app`, described as the version to reach for today and as working on any platform ([official README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut), [opencut.app](https://opencut.app/)).

## 3. Caveats: experimental status and unofficial look-alikes

# OpenCut — Current Architecture and Technology Stack

OpenCut is a free, MIT-licensed open-source video editor for web, desktop and mobile, positioned as “The open-source CapCut alternative” ([repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)).

The critical context for any current stack description is that OpenCut is in a dual-track transition:

- **Classic (stable, in production):** `opencut.app` still runs the classic version, preserved at `opencut-app/opencut-classic` ([repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)).
- **Rewrite (active development):** a ground-up rewrite at `new.opencut.app` with a Rust core, plugin-first architecture, Editor API, MCP server, headless mode and scripting tab ([repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)).

Canonical sources are the monorepo at [OpenCut-app/OpenCut](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut), the system docs at [Architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture) and [Installation](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/installation), product docs at [OpenCut docs](https://opencut.dev/) and [Development docs](https://opencut.dev/docs/development/), and the published WASM package at [opencut-wasm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencut-wasm).

## 1. Frontend and editor architecture

Classic web app:

- **Framework:** Next.js 16 with App Router, React 19, TypeScript ([Architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).
- **UI/styling:** Tailwind CSS 4, Radix UI primitives, Motion for animations ([Architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).
- **Editor core:** singleton `EditorCore` with specialized managers: command, playback, timeline, scenes, project, media, renderer, save, audio, selection ([Architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).
- **Interaction model:** Actions are the trigger/UX layer (toasts, validation, shortcuts); Commands encapsulate undoable mutations; `useEditor()` is required in React, `EditorCore.getInstance()` outside React ([Architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).
- **State:** EditorCore managers + EventEmitter3 observer for editor state; Zustand stores for UI/app state; React local state for component state ([Architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).
- **Editor UI:** Next.js frontend + Timeline Canvas + Preview Panel; multi-track timeline for video/audio/overlay tracks with real-time preview ([OpenCut docs](https://opencut.dev/)).

This matches the classic `apps/web/src/{components,core,hooks,lib,services,stores,types,utils}` layout and `packages/{ui,env}` shared packages ([Architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).

## 2. Backend, data and infrastructure

Classic backend is Next.js-centric with local-first client storage:

- **Database/ORM:** PostgreSQL as primary DB with Drizzle ORM ([Architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).
- **Auth:** Better Auth ([Architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).
- **Cache/rate-limit:** Redis via Upstash Redis REST + `serverless-redis-http` adapter ([Architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).
- **Local dev defaults:** `postgres:17` on `5432`, `redis:7-alpine` on `6379`, serverless Redis HTTP on `8079`; `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://opencut:opencut@localhost:5432/opencut` plus Better Auth secret and Upstash REST URL/token ([Installation](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/installation)).
- **Self-host:** production Docker Compose builds `apps/web/Dockerfile` and runs web + db + redis + serverless-redis-http via `docker compose up -d` on `3100:3000` ([Installation](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/installation)).
- **Tooling:** Turborepo monorepo, Bun runtime/package manager, Biome linter/formatter, Docker ([Architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)) — rewrite adds Moon + Proto orchestration ([repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)).
- **Client storage:** IndexedDB for projects/settings/structured data; OPFS Origin Private File System for large media files via storage abstraction ([OpenCut docs](https://opencut.dev/)).
- **Privacy posture:** local-first; videos stay on device; cloud features opt-in ([Architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).
- **Opt-in cloud integrations:** Cloudflare R2 + Modal URL for auto-captions/transcription, Marble CMS for blog, Databuddy anonymized analytics, Freesound audio library ([Installation](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/installation)).

## 3. Media processing, rendering/export and AI

Transition from browser JS processing to Rust GPU core:

- **Classic processing:** client-side FFmpeg.wasm, WaveSurfer.js waveforms; pipeline documented as FFmpeg.js + background removal + transcription ([Architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).
- **Classic preview problem:** HTML/CSS/Canvas DOM preview is inconsistent with export; in-progress refactor to binary rendering engine for preview/export consistency ([Architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).
- **Rewrite core:** `rust/` is the platform-agnostic single source of truth — GPU compositor, effects, masks and WASM bindings — with business logic migrating from TypeScript; web consumes published `opencut-wasm` (“Shared video editor logic compiled to WebAssembly,” Rust under `rust/crates/`) ([opencut-wasm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencut-wasm)).
- **GPU path:** wgpu compositor with layer/blend/mask WGSL shaders, texture pooling/store, WebGPU with WebGL fallback; desktop is native GPUI sharing the same Rust core; `moon run web:dev / api:dev / desktop:dev` after `proto use` ([repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)).
- **Export/AI services:** canvas + Mediabunny path (MP4/H.264, WebM/VP9, AAC/Opus patterns) and Web Audio decoding are present in recent work; AI/assisted features are integration-based — fal.ai generative image/video/audio sponsor, Python `bg-remover` (U2Net/SAM/Gemini patterns) and transcription service via Modal/Whisper + R2 ([Development docs](https://opencut.dev/docs/development/)).

## Uncertainties and version caveats

- Docs still show both Turborepo (classic) and Moon (rewrite) monorepo descriptions; treat Turborepo + `bun dev:web` as classic and Moon + `proto use` as rewrite ([Architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)) ([repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)).
- Older product docs list Tauri desktop and `apps/bg-remover` + `apps/transcription`; current main lists GPUI desktop and `rust/` core — reflecting classic vs rewrite, not a contradiction in one snapshot ([OpenCut docs](https://opencut.dev/)) ([repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)).
- Exact production hosting for `opencut.app` / `new.opencut.app` edge/CDN was not pinned to primary infra docs beyond self-host Docker and Vercel/fal.ai sponsorship history; self-host Compose is the verified deployment path ([Installation](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/installation)).

claimSummaries.statement: OpenCut is a free MIT-licensed open-source CapCut alternative for web, desktop and mobile.
Canonical codebase is OpenCut-app/OpenCut with legacy stable code at opencut-classic; opencut.app runs classic and new.opencut.app hosts the ground-up rewrite.
Classic web frontend uses Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Radix UI, Zustand and Motion.
Editor architecture centers on a singleton EditorCore with domain managers, actions/commands separation, useEditor hook plus Zustand UI stores and multi-track timeline/preview UI.
Backend uses PostgreSQL with Drizzle ORM, Better Auth, Redis/Upstash caching and rate limiting, built with Bun/Turborepo/Biome/Docker and self-hostable via Docker Compose.
Storage is local-first with IndexedDB for projects/settings and OPFS for media, with opt-in cloud integrations including Cloudflare R2 + Modal transcription, Marble CMS, Databuddy and Freesound.
Classic media processing is client-side via FFmpeg.wasm and WaveSurfer.js, with DOM/HTML/Canvas preview being refactored to a binary/GPU rendering engine for preview-export consistency.

Rewrite moves logic to a Rust platform-agnostic core (wgpu GPU compositor, effects, masks) consumed as opencut-wasm, with GPUI native desktop, Moon/Proto/Bun monorepo tooling, canvas/Mediabunny export, and AI via fal.ai plus bg-remover and transcription services.
